title: Token-pacing governor: clock-synchronous prefill pacing and attention microkernel arbitration for mixed-MIG fleets
creator: Asha Patel
description: Introduce a 'token-pacing governor' that synchronizes prefill pacing to GPU clock headroom and enforces an attention-microkernel arbitration layer for mixed-MIG/HW SKU fleets (H100/L40S/A10). Goal: reduce prefill tail-latency spikes and rocket bursts of clock churn while preserving throughput for common seq-length workloads.
background: We've seen intermittent 95th/99th prefill latency spikes when heterogeneous tenants share MIG-partitioned nodes, especially under bursty short-sequence traffic. The runtime's kernel selection currently prioritizes highest-throughput kernels which can push clocks and MIG slices into transient headroom exhaustion. That leads to asynchronous clock governors and thermal/PCIe contention, increasing token latency and token loss due to prefill-decode handoff jitter.
proposed_solution: Build a lightweight governor that observes per-slice telemetry (clock headroom, sclk, memory bandwidth utilization, MIG occupancy) and applies: (1) clock-synchronous pacing window for prefill request admission, (2) microkernel arbitration that prefers lower-latency attention microkernels when slice headroom is constrained, and (3) burst-smoothing hysteresis to avoid rapid kernel flips. The governor will expose knobs for per-customer QoS tiers and an automated mode that targets configurable latency SLOs.
design_decisions: Use a sliding window token budget computed per-MIG slice rather than global token count to avoid cross-slice starvation.
Prefer latency-optimized microkernels (reduced math throughput) when sclk drops below a threshold; prefer high-throughput kernels at steady-state.
Keep decision logic in runtime's scheduling plane (C++) with a small JS/py shim for configuration so Console can toggle modes without redeploying runtime.
Implement conservative hysteresis (two-tier thresholds) to prevent thrash between kernels during short thermal transients.
Telemetry: sample at 250ms granularity to balance responsiveness and noise; aggregate with exponential smoothing for kernel selection inputs.
acceptance_criteria: 95th-percentile prefill latency reduced by >=20% on mixed workload bench (H100+L40S+A10 MIG splits) compared to baseline runtime-1.23 with same batching config.
No regression in aggregate throughput for 90% of tested seq-length profiles (short/medium/long) beyond 5% relative to baseline.
Kernel-switch events per-minute reduced by >=60% under burst load compared to current opportunistic kernel chooser (reduces clock oscillation).
Configuration knobs available in runtime config and surfaced in Console toggle for 'token-pacing governor' with modes: off / conservative / aggressive.
End-to-end integration tests covering forced headroom drops (synthetic thermal throttling) show graceful fallback and bounded latency.
Safety: when telemetry is missing/unreliable, governor falls back to current kernel-selection policy (no new availability risk).
tasks: Instrument per-MIG slice telemetry channel (sclk, mem bw, occupancy) and add 250ms sampling endpoint
Design token-budget algorithm and hysteresis thresholds; write unit tests
Implement governor decision path in runtime scheduler and microkernel arbitration hook
Expose runtime config flags and integrate with Console feature toggle API
Run bench matrix across H100/L40S/A10 MIG partitions and collect baselines
Iterate thresholds based on bench; produce a rollout plan with canary steps
Create e2e tests to simulate telemetry loss and thermal transients
Prepare rollout playbook and rollback criteria
progress_updates: 2026-03-05: Spike work completed to validate sampling cadence and telemetry schema; initial stash of per-slice sclk + mem_bw metrics available in local telemetry endpoint.
2026-03-07: Token-budget prototype algorithm implemented in scheduler test harness; simple sliding-window budget reduces synthetic 99th prefill by ~18% in lab H100-L40S mixed run.
2026-03-09: Microkernel arbitration hook added to candidate selector; integrated basic hysteresis. Need to refine thresholds for A10 behavior under low-memory headroom.
2026-03-10: Telemetry aggregation smoothing added; beginning full bench sweep across MIG configs (1:1, 2:2, mixed slices).
blockers: Need stable per-slice sclk telemetry from infra agent (currently noisy under heavy multiplexing).
GPU firmware on a small subset of L40S test nodes still reports sclk spikes incorrectly; infra ticket raised.
Coordination with Console team to add toggle before canary rollout (API contract doc pending).
